content.text:
I submitted **index 22** (Fe 0.585, Ni 0.259, V 0.156). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, 9e-8 A. I can't tell how close that is to the best in the library, because I measured only 3 of 160 compositions.

**Why I looked in the Fe-rich corner:** the light is 2.06 eV (602 nm). Of the oxides in this system, only the Fe-rich ones, such as hematite-like oxides and Fe vanadates, have band gaps low enough to absorb at that energy. With only 3 merit measurements, I put all of them there.

**Results:**

| Index | Fe | Ni | V | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **22** | 0.585 | 0.259 | 0.156 | **9e-8** |
| 144 | 0.501 | 0.369 | 0.131 | 4e-8 |
| 61 | 0.516 | 0.209 | 0.274 | 1e-8 |

Photocurrent fell when V was added and also when Fe was swapped for Ni. Index 22 already has the most Fe in the library, so there was no further step in that direction to test.

**Caveats:**
- **Unused budget:** I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements or the GP suggestion tool. So I didn't confirm which phases are present, and the Fe-rich reasoning is an assumption rather than something I checked.
- **Unexplored areas:** the Ni-rich and V-rich regions went completely unmeasured, so I can't rule out a better composition there.
